correction: A regularly kept journal has a direct Hawaiʻi Rule of Evidence 803(b)(6) records-of-regularly-conducted-activity route; the rule is not confined to commercial business records.

legal_authorities_verified_current_run.proposition: A memorandum, report, record, or data compilation in any form may be admitted when made in the course of a regularly conducted activity, at or near the time, through a custodian, qualified witness, or compliant certification, unless circumstances indicate lack of trustworthiness.
Hawaiʻi expanded the formulation beyond business activity to all forms of regularly conducted activity whose records are regularly and reliably prepared and maintained.
A certified record of regularly conducted activity may be self-authenticated when the declaration addresses near-time creation, course of the activity, and regular practice, with advance notice.
Past recollection recorded remains an additional route when the witness once knew the matter, now lacks sufficient recollection, and made or adopted an accurate record while memory was fresh.
Personal-knowledge testimony and refreshed recollection remain additional routes for the same underlying journal material.
